content.title: About
content.content: Almond paste is a thick blend of ground almonds and sugar, sometimes enriched with oil or eggs. It has a sweet, nutty flavor and is used in confectionery as a filling for cakes, cookies, marzipan and other desserts.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Almond paste is the base of traditional marzipan, popular across Europe and the Middle East.
Unlike almond butter, paste retains fine almond particles, giving it a denser texture.
There are two main types: sweet (high sugar) and unsweetened (for a more neutral taste).
It is often used in gluten‑free recipes as a flour substitute.
In Italy, almond paste is traditionally served with panettone during the holidays.

items.title: Rich in vitamin E
items.content: Almond paste retains much of the vitamin E found in almonds, an antioxidant that protects cells from oxidative stress.

items.title: Provides healthy monounsaturated fats
items.content: Monounsaturated fats support heart health and can improve lipid profiles.

items.title: Contains magnesium
items.content: Magnesium supports normal muscle and nerve function.

items.title: Provides protein and fiber
items.content: The paste supplies plant protein and dietary fiber, helping promote satiety.

items.title: Source of calcium
items.content: It contains calcium, important for bone and teeth health.

items.title: Tree nut allergy
items.content: Almond paste can trigger allergic reactions in individuals sensitive to nuts.

items.title: High in calories
items.content: Because of its fat and sugar content, portion sizes should be moderated.

items.title: Sugar content
items.content: The sweet version may raise blood glucose levels, so people with diabetes should opt for unsweetened paste.

items.title: Oxalate content
items.content: Almonds contain oxalates, which can contribute to kidney stone formation in susceptible individuals.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Almond paste is used as a filling for cakes, cupcakes, cookies, in marzipan, as well as in creams and glazes. It can be mixed with fruit purées, added to dough, or melted for drizzling over desserts.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Store the paste in an airtight container in the refrigerator for up to 3 months. For longer storage, freeze it for up to 6 months. Before use, check for off‑odors or signs of spoilage.

content.title: About
content.content: A bagel is a ring-shaped bread made from yeasted dough that is briefly boiled in water before being baked. Traditionally associated with Jewish cuisine, bagels are now enjoyed worldwide. They feature a dense, slightly chewy crust and a soft, airy interior.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: The modern bagel is believed to have originated in Poland in the 17th century and was brought to the United States by Jewish immigrants.
Traditional preparation includes a short boil in water with added baking soda or milk, giving the bagel its characteristic glossy crust.
Bagels are often served with smoked salmon, cream cheese, red onion, and capers – the classic “lox and bagel”.
There are many flavor variations, from classic sesame and poppy seed to sweet versions with cinnamon, raisins, or chocolate.
In the United States more than 1.5 billion bagels are sold each year.

items.title: Source of complex carbohydrates
items.content: Bagels made with whole‑grain flour provide sustained energy through slowly digestible carbs.

items.title: Contains dietary fiber
items.content: Fiber supports healthy digestion and helps maintain a feeling of fullness.

items.title: Rich in B‑vitamins
items.content: B1, B2, and niacin aid carbohydrate metabolism and support the nervous system.

items.title: Provides iron
items.content: Iron is essential for oxygen transport in the blood and overall energy levels.

items.title: Low in added sugar
items.content: Unlike many sweet pastries, a plain bagel contains minimal added sugars.

items.title: High calorie density
items.content: Because a bagel is a dense bread, a single serving can be calorie‑rich; portion control is advisable for weight management.

items.title: Gluten content
items.content: Bagels made from wheat flour are unsuitable for people with celiac disease or gluten sensitivity.

items.title: Sodium
items.content: Traditional bagels are often topped with coarse salt, which may be a concern for those with hypertension.

items.title: Added sugars in sweet varieties
items.content: Sweet bagels with raisins, chocolate, or glaze can raise the glycemic index.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Slice a bagel in half and toast it, then spread with cream cheese, avocado, hummus, or sliced meats. It also works well as a sandwich base for salmon, egg, and vegetables. Sweet bagels are enjoyed with jam, honey, or chocolate spread.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Keep bagels in a paper bag at room temperature for up to 2 days to retain a crisp crust. For longer storage, place them in an airtight container and refrigerate for up to 5 days or freeze for up to 2 months.

content.title: About
content.content: Fried dough is a piece of dough that is deep‑fried until golden and crisp. It is a common component of street food, snacks, and desserts. The dough is usually made from wheat flour, water, yeast, and a touch of sugar, shaped into small pieces and quickly fried in hot oil.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Fried dough is popular worldwide, from American "fair dough" to Indian "puri" and Russian "ponchiki".
The hot oil causes the dough to puff up rapidly, creating a crunchy crust and a light, airy interior.
In many countries it is served with powdered sugar, honey, chocolate sauce, or savory fillings.
Traditional frying uses high‑smoke‑point vegetable oils such as sunflower or canola oil.
In the US fried dough is a staple at fairs and carnivals, often marketed as "fair food".

items.title: Source of carbohydrates
items.content: The dough provides quick‑acting carbs that replenish energy after physical activity.

items.title: Contains some protein
items.content: Wheat flour supplies plant‑based protein needed for tissue repair.

items.title: B‑vitamins
items.content: Fried dough contains thiamine, niacin, and folate, which support energy metabolism.

items.title: Minerals
items.content: It provides iron, magnesium, and phosphorus, important for blood and bone health.

items.title: Easy to digest
items.content: When properly prepared, fried dough is gentle on the stomach and suitable for a quick snack.

items.title: High fat content
items.content: Deep‑frying adds significant calories and saturated fat.

items.title: High glycemic index
items.content: Rapid carbs can cause a quick spike in blood sugar, which is undesirable for people with diabetes.

items.title: Gluten allergy
items.content: Wheat‑based dough contains gluten and is not suitable for those with celiac disease or gluten sensitivity.

items.title: Trans fats from reused oil
items.content: Reusing frying oil can generate trans fats, which are harmful to cardiovascular health.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Serve fried dough hot, dusted with powdered sugar, cinnamon, or salt. It can be filled with sweet toppings (chocolate, jam) or savory fillings (cheese, sausage). It is often accompanied by dipping sauces such as honey‑mustard, chocolate, or tomato sauce.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Fried dough is best enjoyed immediately after cooking. If you need to store it, let it cool to room temperature, place it in an airtight container, and keep it for 1‑2 days. Reheat in the oven before serving to restore crispness.

egg-sandwich-on-croissant-with-sausage.title: Egg sandwich on croissant with sausage

content.title: About
content.content: The egg sandwich on croissant with sausage is a tasty breakfast or snack where a buttery croissant is filled with a soft boiled egg and flavorful sausage. The croissant provides a light, crisp crust while the egg and sausage deliver protein and a rich taste.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: The croissant originated in Austria but became iconic in France, where it is often used as a sandwich base.
Eggs are usually hard‑boiled for this sandwich so they stay intact while eating.
The sausage can vary from classic boiled to smoked, allowing flavor customization.
The combination of pastry, egg, and meat offers a balanced mix of protein, fat, and carbs.
This sandwich is commonly served in cafés and bistros as a quick morning bite.

items.title: Rich in protein
items.content: Eggs and sausage provide high‑quality protein essential for muscle repair and satiety.

items.title: Source of B‑vitamins
items.content: Eggs contain vitamin B12, while sausage adds niacin and riboflavin, supporting energy metabolism.

items.title: Contains iron
items.content: Meat‑based sausage, especially beef, supplies heme iron, which aids oxygen transport.

items.title: Energy boost
items.content: The croissant supplies quick‑release carbohydrates for morning energy.

items.title: Provides calcium
items.content: Croissant dough made with milk adds a modest amount of calcium for bone health.

items.title: High in fats and calories
items.content: Croissants and sausage are rich in saturated fats; moderate consumption is advised for weight‑watching individuals.

items.title: Sodium content
items.content: Processed sausage often contains a lot of salt, which can be problematic for hypertension.

items.title: Egg allergy
items.content: People with egg allergy should avoid this sandwich.

items.title: Preservatives in sausage
items.content: Some sausages contain nitrites and other additives; choose nitrate‑free options when possible.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: The sandwich is easy to eat by hand, preferably cut in half. It pairs well with a side salad, fresh tomato slices, or a dab of mustard for extra flavor.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Store the assembled sandwich in an airtight container in the refrigerator for up to 24 hours. For longer storage, keep the components separate and re‑warm the croissant before serving.

infant-formula-gerber-good-start-soy-sta.title: Infant formula, Gerber Good Start Soy, Stage 1, powder, made with bottled water (375)

content.title: About
content.content: Gerber Good Start Soy Stage 1 is a soy‑based infant formula designed for babies from birth to 6 months (Stage 1). The powder is reconstituted with water, in this case bottled water, ensuring purity and consistent composition. The formula provides plant protein, DHA, ARA, prebiotics and essential vitamins needed for growth and development.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Suitable for infants who need a soy alternative to cow’s milk.
Contains DHA and ARA – fatty acids that support brain and eye development.
Prebiotics in the formula help promote a healthy gut microbiome.
Each container yields multiple servings, making it convenient for travel.
Gerber Good Start Soy has undergone clinical testing for safety and tolerance in infants.

items.title: Supports brain development
items.content: DHA and ARA are critical components for the formation of neural tissue and visual system.

items.title: Easy to digest
items.content: Soy protein is hypoallergenic and generally well tolerated by infants with lactose intolerance.

items.title: Immune support
items.content: Vitamins A, C, D and zinc help strengthen the infant’s immune defenses.

items.title: Promotes healthy gut flora
items.content: Prebiotic fructooligosaccharides stimulate the growth of beneficial bacteria in the intestine.

items.title: Provides energy
items.content: The formula supplies carbohydrates and fats needed for growth and activity.

items.title: Soy allergy
items.content: Some infants may develop an allergic reaction to soy proteins; discontinue use at the first sign of symptoms.

items.title: Not suitable for phenylketonuria
items.content: The formula contains phenylalanine, so it must not be given to children with PKU.

items.title: Proper reconstitution required
items.content: Incorrect water‑to‑powder ratio can lead to dehydration or nutrient excess.

items.title: Storage after opening
items.content: Keep the opened container in a dry place and use within the stated period; otherwise taste and safety may deteriorate.

content.title: How to Prepare
content.content: Use clean bottled water warmed to about 37 °C (body temperature). Add the measured amount of powder (usually 1 scoop per 30 ml of water), mix thoroughly until smooth. Prepare the feed immediately and do not leave it at room temperature for more than 1 hour.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Store the dry powder in its original sealed container in a cool, dry place away from direct sunlight. After opening, use within 30 days. Do not keep prepared formula at room temperature for longer than 1 hour.
